title: How a Mobile Flooring Showroom Works: Picking Hardwood in Your Own Everett Living Room
meta: A mobile flooring showroom brings hardwood planks to your Everett home, measures, checks the subfloor and quotes on the spot. How a Wills Flooring visit goes.

blocks.lead: A mobile flooring showroom means the showroom comes to you: we bring full-size hardwood samples to your Everett home, lay them on your floor in your light, measure every room, check the subfloor and hand you a firm written quote before we leave.
blocks.detail: The visit is free and takes about an hour. Installation labor is published at $3.25 per sq ft for engineered or solid hardwood and $2.75 for unfinished, with a 500 sq ft minimum. Material is quoted from the samples you pick.

blocks.html: People search "flooring store near me" in Everett, drive to a warehouse, stand under fluorescent lights holding a 4-inch chip, and then wonder at home why the floor looks nothing like the chip. A mobile showroom skips all of that. Wills Flooring has run one since 2013 from our Lynnwood location on 196th St SW, and Everett is our closest big service area. Here is what happens when we pull up in Silver Lake, Riverside or a Port Gardner condo, what we check, and how to get the most out of the hour.

blocks.text: What happens during the visit, step by step

items.text: You tell us the rooms, whether there is carpet or old flooring to remove, and the look you are after. We load the van with samples that fit: white oak, hickory, maple, a few engineered and solid options in the tones you mentioned.
items.note: Two or three photos by text help us bring the right boards.

items.text: We lay full planks on your floor, not chips. You see the color next to your cabinets, your trim and the gray Everett light coming through the windows. We move them room to room.
We measure every room, closet and hallway with a laser, sketch the layout and note stairs, transitions and doorways. Square footage goes on the quote to the foot.

We pull a register or lift a corner of carpet to see what is under it: plywood, OSB, planks or slab. We check flatness with a straightedge and moisture with a meter. Surprises get caught now, not on install day.
You get a written quote with labor, the material you picked, removal, prep and stairs as separate lines. It is firm. If you want to sleep on it, the number does not change next week.

blocks.text: Why seeing the wood in your Everett house matters

items.title: Everett light is not showroom light
items.text: A north-facing Bayside living room in January gets flat, blue-gray daylight. A greige white oak that looked warm under store LEDs can read cold and washed out here. On your floor at 3 pm on a cloudy day you see the truth.

items.title: Your trim and cabinets are the real test
items.text: Silver Lake and Eastmont homes from the 1990s and 2000s often have honey-oak cabinets and stair rails. A new floor has to sit next to those, not next to a showroom wall. We hold the plank against the cabinet toe kick and you decide in seconds.

items.title: Full planks show the real grain
items.text: A 4-inch chip shows one board. A 7-inch by 48-inch plank shows knots, mineral streaks and color variation across a box. Hickory in particular looks tame on a chip and busy on a floor.

items.title: We carry what we install
items.text: Wills Flooring is a Metropolitan Hardwood distributor, so the samples in the van are lines we install every week and can price on the spot, not a catalog we have never laid.

blocks.text: Mobile showroom vs driving to a store

blocks.text: Mistakes people make when choosing hardwood at home

items.html: Deciding at night under warm bulbs. Everett sunsets are at 4:30 in December. Book a daytime slot, or keep two finalist planks overnight and look again in the morning.
Judging from one plank. Ask to see three or four boards from the same line spread out. If the variation bothers you on four boards, it will bother you on four hundred.
Ignoring the subfloor result. If the meter reads high, the answer is to fix the crawlspace ventilation or wait, not to pick a different color. We will say so even if it delays the job.

Comparing our labor to a bundled price. Our $3.25 per sq ft is labor only. A competing "$9 installed" quote may or may not include removal, prep, stairs and moldings. Line them up item by item. Here is what a complete quote should list.
Forgetting the stairs. Hardwood on stairs is $125 per stair. An Eastmont two-story with 14 steps adds $1,750 in labor, and the treads should be picked at the same visit so they match.

blocks.text: How to get the most out of the hour

items.title: Clear a 6 ft patch of floor
items.text: We need a spot in the main room and one in the kitchen to lay planks. Moving a rug is enough. If there is carpet, a spot where we can lift a corner near a wall helps too.

items.title: Save three inspiration photos
items.text: Even if the photos are of very different floors, the pattern tells us what you like: wide and pale, or narrow and warm. It cuts the sample stack from twenty to five.

items.title: Have the decision-makers home
items.text: If two people are choosing, both should see the planks in the same light. A phone photo of a plank sent to a spouse is the number one cause of a second visit.

items.title: Know your timeline
items.text: Boeing shift changes, a listing date or a baby due in March all change what we recommend. Engineered ships faster than some solid lines, and unfinished site-finished floors add a week of sanding and finish.

faq.q: Is the mobile showroom visit really free in Everett?
faq.a: Yes. There is no charge and no obligation for the in-home visit anywhere in Everett or the rest of Snohomish and King County. We bring samples, measure, check the subfloor and leave a written quote. You can call back in a week or a year.

faq.q: Can I still visit the Lynnwood showroom instead?
faq.a: Of course. The showroom is at 2109 196th St SW #106 in Lynnwood, about 15 minutes from most of Everett. Many customers browse there first, then have us bring two or three finalists to the house to see them in their own light.

faq.q: How many hardwood samples do you bring?
faq.a: Usually 10 to 20 full planks chosen from what you describe on the phone, across engineered and solid white oak, hickory, maple and a few stained options. If nothing lands, we schedule a second visit with a different set at no charge.

faq.q: Do you quote material and labor together?
faq.a: The quote lists them separately so you can see both. Labor is our published $3.25 per sq ft for engineered or solid, or $2.75 for unfinished plus refinishing rates. Material is priced from the plank you picked. Removal and prep are their own lines.

faq.q: What if my subfloor fails the moisture check?
faq.a: We tell you and put a number on the fix or a wait period. In Everett the usual causes are a wet crawlspace or a slab without a vapor barrier. Installing hardwood over a wet subfloor voids the manufacturer warranty, so we will not do it.

faq.q: How soon after the visit can you install?
faq.a: Most Everett installs are scheduled two to four weeks after you accept the quote, depending on material lead time. In-stock engineered lines can be quicker. Site-finished unfinished floors add about a week for sanding and three coats.
